# Extract Frames from Video

- Route: `/tools/extract-frames-from-video`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `extract-frames-from-video`

## Summary

Pull still image frames out of any video — every N seconds, at a target frame rate, or at specific timestamps — and download them as a ZIP. (Video tools)

## Details

Frame extraction turns a video back into a sequence of still images — useful for thumbnails, reference shots, design mockups, ML datasets, and animation/storyboard previews. Media Manipulator lets you sample frames every N seconds, at a target frame rate, or at specific timestamps, and packages the resulting images into a single ZIP for download.
### What it does
- Extracts still frames as JPG, PNG, or WebP images.
- Supports three sampling modes: every N seconds, target frames per second, or specific timestamps.
- Packages the frames into a single ZIP for one-click download.
- Enforces a max-frame guardrail so runs stay fast and predictable.
### How to use it
1. Upload your video: Drop any MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, AVI, or M4V file.
2. Pick a sampling mode: Every N seconds, a target FPS, or a comma-separated list of timestamps.
3. Choose image format: JPG for compact thumbnails, PNG for lossless stills, WebP for smaller modern files.
4. Download ZIP: All extracted frames are packaged into a single .zip you can extract anywhere.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi, m4v
- Output: zip (containing jpg/png/webp frames)
- Default max-frame cap is 300 — raise it up to 1000 in the form if you really need more.
- Timestamp mode accepts a comma-separated list of seconds (e.g. "1, 5.5, 12.25, 30").
### Technical details
- Every-N-seconds and FPS modes use FFmpeg’s fps filter to sample evenly across the timeline.
- Timestamp mode runs one FFmpeg invocation per requested timestamp so per-frame failures (out-of-bounds requests, etc.) surface clearly.
- The max-frame guardrail defaults to 300 and caps at 1000 — keeps jobs fast and avoids runaway extractions.
### Use cases
- Thumbnails and previews: Pick a single frame to use as a YouTube/Vimeo thumbnail.
- Design references: Sample a sequence of frames from gameplay or animation as drawing reference.
- Storyboards: Generate a sequence of key frames for a storyboard pitch.
- ML datasets: Build small image datasets from a small number of videos quickly.
### FAQ
Q: How do I extract frames from a video?
A: Upload your video, pick a sampling mode (every N seconds is the default), choose an image format, and click "Extract frames". The result is a ZIP of still images.
Q: Can I export one frame every few seconds?
A: Yes — that is the default mode. Set "Seconds between frames" to whatever interval you want.
Q: What image formats are supported?
A: JPG (compact, ideal for thumbnails), PNG (lossless), and WebP (smaller modern files).
Q: Why does the tool return a ZIP file?
A: Even short videos can produce dozens of frames. Returning a single ZIP keeps the download to one click and avoids fighting the browser over multiple file downloads.
Q: Why is there a max-frame limit?
A: The limit prevents accidental runaway jobs (e.g. extracting tens of thousands of frames from a long video). The default is 300 and the absolute cap is 1000.
